newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill rates softer but trading subdued.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill rates softer but trading subdued.

text.p: Treasury bill rates at the secondary market mellowed on Monday but trading remained sudued ahead of the auction, traders said.

"Rates have softened because of the volume in the auction," a trader said. The Bureau of Treasury cut down by half its T-bill volume to 2.5 billion pesos in view of the prevailing high interest rates.

Banks continue to hunt for T-bills but there were few sellers in the market, the trader said, adding some of these banks would only want to sell the long-term T-bonds which do not offer attractive rates.
"I'd rather stay short of bills for now," the dealer said.
He said he would wait for Tuesday's sale of 35- and 45-day cash management bills which may yield higher rates.
Moreover, banks still have to contend with the high carrying cost for T-bills with the central bank overnight borrowing rate at 25 percent, the trader added.
A Reuters poll of six financial institutions gave bids of 13.5/14 percent for the three-month bills; 14/14.5 percent for the six months; and 14.5/15.0 for the one-year bills.
The average interbank call loan rate was unchanged at 25.09375 percent, with done rates from 28 percent to 25.03125 percent.
Volume was higher at 13.94 billion pesos from 9.05 billion as banks covered their weekend positions.
Out of the 41 participating financial institutions, 28 were lenders.
